label: womotte2
title: 〜をもって (を以て)
meaning: By means of, via, through - method by which you do / achieve something 道具や手段を表す。〜で。

notes.text: Ref # Kanzen Master Level 1 - p71 - no.68

On the difference between  and 

 is a Time phrase

meaning "at"  - marks beginnings, ends, or borders between times.

It is often used as a greeting to お客 with the extended form  をもちまして.

 is the method by which you do something - victory achieved via effort, announcement made via a blackboard.



Both are formal, both are NOUN + をもって

be careful.
notes.html:
On the difference between  and 
 is a Time phrase
meaning "at" - marks beginnings, ends, or borders between times.
It is often used as a greeting to お客 with the extended form をもちまして.
 is the method by which you do something - victory achieved via effort, announcement made via a blackboard.

Both are formal, both are NOUN + をもって
be careful.

		with his amazing efforts, we were able to get the champion's cup

examples.japanese: こんな難問は、優秀な彼の頭脳をもってしても解決できないだろう。
examples.body_text:
こんな難問は、優秀な彼の頭脳をもってしても解決できないだろう。  

		Even with his brilliant mind, such a difficult problem cannot be resolved.
examples.body_html:
こんな難問は、優秀な彼の頭脳をもってしても解決できないだろう。  
Even with his brilliant mind, such a difficult problem cannot be resolved.

examples.japanese: 彼の迫ﾍをもってすれば，この問題の解決は容易であろう
examples.body_text:
彼の迫ﾍをもってすれば，この問題の解決は容易であろう 

		With his ability, he should be able to solve the problem easily.
